destination.name: K'gari
destination.tagline: A World Heritage sand island of freshwater lakes and rainforest on the dunes
destination.description: K'gari, formerly Fraser Island, is a sand island about 122 km long off Queensland's southern coast, and was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1992. Most of it is Great Sandy National Park. The main beach doubles as a highway for 4WDs, passing Eli Creek, the SS Maheno wreck and Indian Head, while coloured sand cliffs and more than 100 freshwater lakes lie inland. Dingoes live wild here, and visitors must keep food secured and never feed them.
whyVisit: Drive the beach highway in a 4WD
Walk rainforest growing on sand dunes
Spot rays, turtles and dolphins from headlands

goodToKnow.title: Vehicle permit required
goodToKnow.detail: Every vehicle needs a permit on the windscreen, and campers outside commercial campgrounds need a camping permit. Get both before you go.

goodToKnow.title: 4WD and barge only
goodToKnow.detail: Vehicles cross by barge from River Heads or Inskip Point, and the sand roads need a 4WD. Allow about three days, or take a guided tour if unsure.

goodToKnow.title: Stay dingo safe
goodToKnow.detail: Feeding dingoes is fined. Lock food away when unattended, and skip ocean swimming, where surf and sharks are a risk.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} are the dry, mild months, with humpback whales passing in Jul–Aug.
